minutes.headline: Capital Planning Committee reviewed the FY capital list without voting on it, asked for a yearly asset inventory, and approved prior minutes.
minutes.summary: The committee discussed a bylaw-based town asset inventory, then went through concerns on the roughly 29-item capital request list: Flat Hill Road drainage, the cemetery, the Eagle House parking lot, DPW dump trucks, a public safety office/canine building and school safety projects. It agreed on a scoring method and next meeting dates. The only votes were approving minutes and adjourning.

public_comment.topic: Resident questioned spending on school safety window film and security upgrades, argued for expanding the school resource officer program instead, and said she could not support the items without more information.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of October 17th and October 26th (captions say 22nd).
Adjourn until Wednesday November 30 at 6 p.m.

decisions.decision: Chair will raise the annual asset inventory with the town manager, aiming to have it early in the process, with added and retired items marked.
Members will rank the capital items 1 to 29 and submit scores only to the chair, who will tabulate them in a spreadsheet; summed as last year.
Chair will ask the DPW director, copying the town manager, about the cemetery project and whether Flat Hill Road is engineering or construction.
Next meetings set for November 30 and December 14.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee took no votes on the capital request list; the only votes were to approve prior minutes and to adjourn.
Members agreed to rank each item on the roughly 29-item request list and send scores only to the chair, who will tabulate them as last year.
Members questioned the Eagle House parking lot, the DPW dump trucks, the ambulance funding source and the Flat Hill Road drainage project; none was resolved.
The chair will ask the town manager for a yearly town asset inventory, with added and retired items marked, early in the process.
A resident questioned school safety window film and security items and argued for expanding the school resource officer program instead.

why_it_matters: The committee's ranking of capital items is advisory and still unscored, so which projects reach a town meeting vote, and how they are paid for, is not yet settled.
Several items drew open questions about funding source (the special purpose stabilization fund, free cash or borrowing), which decides whether a project is paid from savings or from the tax levy.
watch_next: Committee meetings set for November 30 and December 14, when the ranked capital list is expected to be tabulated.
